fixes.title: Captured Images grades dark/calibration frames as "Good", inflating the session quality summary
fixes.summary: FrameQualityAssessmentService.assessFrame walks DOWN from an advisory 75 and is only ever decremented by a metric, so a frame with hfr/starCount/guidingRmsTotal/qualityScore all null comes back FrameQualityLevel.good with a 75 score. image_thumbnail_strip.dart now only hands the assessor frames it can judge (_hasQualityMeasurement), counts the rest in a new neutral 'Unrated' chip, keeps 'Total' as the real frame count, and badges those tiles UNRATED with a tooltip naming the four missing metrics instead of a green GOOD. The strip is the only analytics consumer; the other two call sites of assessBatch are in screens/session_review and are listed as a shared change.

The lights are seeded at hfr 2.6 / guiding 1.4" - the heuristic's own fallback values - because that is what makes an unmeasured dark score identically to a real light, which is the live case.

fixes.title: Recovering a stale session stamps end_time = now, inflating its duration by days
fixes.summary: Confirmed present and unfixed. The verifier's correction is right: session_service.dart:431 is only the scan; the write is markSessionAborted (session_service.dart:538-545) -> ImagingRecordsRepository.endSession -> packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/database/daos/sessions_dao.dart:108-115, whose body is `endTime: Value(DateTime.now())` with no way for a caller to say otherwise. Neither file is in my ownership list (I own only images_dao and science_dao), so I did not edit them. My session-elapsed work for findings 1 and 3 does NOT paper over this: it only chooses an honest figure while end_time is NULL, and once recovery stamps `now` the row looks like a legitimately closed 60-hour session everywhere.

DateTime.now())`. (2) The same optional parameter through ImagingRecordsRepository.endSession (imaging_records_repository.dart:181). (3) session_service.dart markSessionAborted: close an abandoned session at its last frame, not at the clock - `final last = await _imagesDao.getLastCapturedAtForSession(sessionId); await _records.endSession(sessionId, status: 'aborted', endTime: (last != null && last.isAfter(session.startTime)) ? last : session.startTime);`. fixes.title: Science guide ladder is stuck on rung 1 while the same page plots an 80-point curve, a period and an Export button
fixes.summary: evaluateLadder computed every rung from the state of the rung above it, so one missing photometric calibration cascaded four locks: track locked -> curve locked -> period locked -> contribute locked, no matter what the session actually contained. Each rung is now judged on its OWN evidence: track is done when the session has photometry points (or live tracking) and is never locked, since picking a star needs nothing first; curve is done at >=10 points; period is done when a result exists; contribute is ready whenever there is exportable data. The three prerequisite strings in science_ladder_card.dart were rewritten to match the one condition that can now lock each rung - the old 'Turn on live photometry...' and 'Find a period... before exporting' lines described the cascade, not the state.
fixes.test: 'the light-curve rung is not padlocked over an 80-point curve', 'the contribute rung offers its export when data exists' and 'evidence beats the cascade' in packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/analytics/widgets/science_ladder_evidence_test.dart - renders ScienceLadderCard with the audit's exact inputs (80 points, a period result, exportable data, NO calibration) and opens rungs 3 and 5.
fixes.revert_check: Restored the two cascade branches (`if (measure != done) track = locked` and `if (track == locked) curve = locked`); the widget test failed with 'Found 1 widget with text containing start collecting points' and the model test with 'Actual: RungState.locked'. Restored, green (23 tests).
fixes.caveats: Two assertions in the pre-existing science_ladder_model_test.dart encoded the old cascade for the track rung ('locked until calibration'); they now assert the new contract, with a comment saying why. That is a deliberate contract change, not a weakened test - the surrounding 18 assertions are untouched.

fixes.title: BLS card gives no significance verdict, and its SDE scores pure noise higher than a strong periodic signal
fixes.summary: The ordering defect is real and is NOT fixed: I re-read period_analysis_service.dart:604-621 and the statistic is computed over the whole SR spectrum, peak included, so a coherent signal inflates its own baseline mean and std and deflates its own SDE. (I checked the one thing that would have been a cheap unit bug - srSpectrum[ip] is already sqrt'ed at :557 and peakSr is sqrt(globalBestSr) at :620, so the units DO match; the problem is the unmasked baseline, not a scale error.) That file is outside my ownership. What I did fix is the half that is mine: the BLS column printed a bare 'SDE: 3.1' with no threshold, so a user comparing two runs would rank 2.6 below 3.1. It now reads 'SDE: 3.1 (below the 6.0 significance threshold; compare SDE only within one light curve)'.
fixes.test: The threshold assertion is in 'every tick on both spectrum axes carries a distinct value' (periodogram_axis_labels_test.dart), which renders the panel over a real analysis result.
fixes.revert_check: Restored the bare 'SDE: ${sde.toStringAsFixed(1)}' detail string; the test failed with 'Found 0 widgets with text containing significance threshold'. Restored, green.
fixes.caveats: The label makes the number honest; it does NOT make the number right. A genuine injected transit still only reaches SDE 4.8 on this implementation and will read 'below the threshold'.
fixes.needs_shared_change: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/science/period_analysis_service.dart:604-621. Exclude the peak's own neighbourhood from the baseline before computing mean/std - standard BLS-SDE practice: find `peakIndex` (the trial whose srSpectrum entry equals peakSr), build the baseline from trials whose period differs from globalBestPeriod by more than ~20% (or simply outside +/- nTrials/20 indices), and compute srMean/srStd over that subset only, falling back to the full spectrum when fewer than ~20 trials survive. Verify with the three controlled 80-point curves from the finding (pure noise, injected 20-min sinusoid amplitude 0.10 mag, injected box transit depth 0.150 mag at P=20 min): the ordering must become noise < sinusoid < transit, and the transit must clear the 6.0 threshold the service's own doc comment at :81 states. Once it does, period_analysis_panel.dart:592-599's Strong/Noteworthy badge starts firing and the 'compare SDE only within one light curve' caveat I added can be dropped.

fixes.title: Diagnostics tab shows loading skeletons forever for a session it cannot analyse
fixes.summary: Confirmed present and unfixed, and the verifier's diagnosis holds up on inspection: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/optical_train_diagnostics_provider.dart:31-38 composes with the deprecated `ref.watch(provider.stream)`, which forwards only FUTURE events. When the Science tab has already subscribed to sessionPsfTilesProvider(id) / sessionResidualVectorsProvider(id) the source has already emitted its only value, so the derived StreamProviders never emit, psfAsync/residualsAsync stay isLoading and :65-67 returns AsyncValue.loading() forever - which is exactly why only the session the user had just viewed in Science hangs. That file is a core provider, not mine, and no change inside the Analytics screen could fix it without relocating the defect (a UI timeout would replace an indefinite skeleton with a false error).

fixes.needs_shared_change: Delete the stream re-wrapping entirely. Replace psfTilesForSessionProvider / residualVectorsForSessionProvider with plain providers that forward the AsyncValue: `final psfTilesForSessionProvider = Provider.autoDispose.family<AsyncValue<List<PsfFieldTileRow>>, int>((ref, sessionId) => ref.watch(sessionPsfTilesProvider(sessionId)));` and likewise for residuals, then drop _watchScienceRows and its `// ignore: deprecated_member_use`. opticalTrainDiagnosticsProvider already consumes AsyncValues and needs no change. Suggested test: read sessionPsfTilesProvider(id) to completion first (the Science-tab-then-Diagnostics order), THEN read opticalTrainDiagnosticsProvider(id) and assert it resolves to data rather than staying loading - that ordering is the whole defect and a test that subscribes to the diagnostics provider first will pass either way.

UniformityTrendCard now takes rejectedImageIds and drops metric rows whose captured_image_id was rejected (rows with no image link stay, since they cannot be attributed), and science_analytics_tab.dart passes the rejected ids from the same lightFrames list the HFR card gets. Both subtitles now state the population ('Accepted frames only (N rejected, not plotted).'), and the HFR empty state says the true reason - 'No accepted frames with star metrics - 2 frames with HFR were rejected.' - instead of sending the user after a star-detection problem that does not exist.

fixes.title: Photometry CSV export writes local wall-clock timestamps with no timezone
fixes.summary: All seven CSV builders called toIso8601String() on the LOCAL DateTime drift returns for a unix-seconds column, so a 09:00 UTC measurement exported as '2026-08-01T05:00:00.000' with no offset and no Z on this UTC-4 host. Added _utcStamp() (toUtc().toIso8601String(), always ending in Z) and routed all seven through it; the column header is now 'Timestamp (UTC)'. Added a JD column to the photometry export (_julianDate), since that is the time system AAVSO/AID submissions and the period analysis actually use. The two export FILENAME stamps were local too - they now use UTC with a trailing Z so a file exported at 00:30 local is not filed under the wrong night.
fixes.test: 'photometry CSV timestamps are UTC and carry a JD column' in the same file. The seeded row's timestamp is DateTime.fromMillisecondsSinceEpoch(...) - LOCAL-flagged, which is what drift hands back - so the assertion is timezone-independent: on a UTC host the old code still omits the Z.
fixes.revert_check: Changed the photometry row back to `m.timestamp.toIso8601String()`; the test failed (the CSV carried '2026-08-01T05:00:00.000'). Restored, green together with the pre-existing science_export_hub_session_state_test.dart (5 tests).
